rule: A prediction is correct when it matches the label (TRUE->TRUE, FALSE->FALSE). MISLEADING counts as correct for FALSE claims. UNVERIFIED is an abstention and counts as not correct in accuracy; 'accuracy when answered' leaves abstentions out.
description: 46 human-labeled claims (half TRUE, half FALSE) across science, health, history, geography and technology. Both modes judge the same sources and verified quotes: the single mode uses only the fast model's verdict, the jury adds an independent Nemotron Ultra verdict and a debate round when they disagree. MISLEADING counts as correct for FALSE claims; UNVERIFIED is an abstention.
